text:
Noah: FYI seeing a sudden CPU p99 spike on telemetry-collector after yesterday's routing tweak. collector CPU p99 went from ~220ms to ~760ms for span processing, host cpu sits at 82%.
Priya: ugh. is this for all tenants or a subset? :eyes: 
Noah: looks concentrated on a single backend pool (us-west-2, routing policy change to favor small requests), but exporter queue growth is cluster-wide. I grabbed a few counters:
Noah: ```
otel_collector.process_time.p99 = 760ms
exporter.queue.size = 18732
exporter.queue.max_seen = 19450
span_ingest.rate = +2.9x
```
Sam: exporter.queue.size that high is bad. did batching params change or did we change sampling recently?
Lee: we rolled routing policy yesterday to divert low-throughput sessions to the new dedicated pool (experiment). nothing touched sampling configs.
Priya: could routing change cause span duplication? I remember the new pool does a sidecar that reattaches trace context in some cases.
Noah: yep found many repeated span.attributes.trace_reattached=true and span length increased (extra attrs). shows extra 5-10 attrs per span which amplifies payload.
Ashley: any idea why queue builds up rather than export backpressureing earlier?
Noah: exporter backoff is kicking but our exporter uses long batch windows for efficiency (batch_size=128, batch_timeout=200ms). with smaller spans multiplied, batch fills slower but CPU per span still high b/c of attribute overhead. also KV cache prefix-caching seems to cause additional attribute expansion when we enrich spans in pipeline.
Sam: quick mitigation: reduce batch_size to 32 and batch_timeout to 80ms, and force exporter concurrency down to 2 to reduce CPU thrash. also enable attribute trimming filter.
Lee: can we run that as a canary on just the problematic pool? deploy-bot, can we patch collector config on ns telemetry-canary
deploy-bot: deploy request: patch config telemetry-collector/us-west-2/canary — queued, will apply to 1 node. CI checks OK.
Priya: I can add a pipeline filter to drop repeated_reattach and trim heavy headers: processor.filter(attributes, include=[], exclude=["http.headers.*","cookie"]) — will try in canary.
Noah: trying the canary now. early numbers after 5m: exporter.queue.size -> 3200, p99 process_time -> 310ms. still above baseline but much better.
Ashley: good. what's causing the original surge? need root cause — is it routing->sidecar->attr explosion or retention/TTL backlog causing retries?
Noah: hypothesis: routing moved a large number of short-lived sessions through the legacy sidecar adapter, which double-tags spans while the collector's prefix cache expands KV sets leading to extra CPU when serializing. also retention service reported a small spike in pending writes to S3 (TTL job lag), which slows exporter ack and increases queue depth.
Sam: action items: (1) keep canary config for 1h, (2) push attribute trim + batch tune to canary cluster, (3) add a dashboard tile for exporter.queue.* and attr_count.hist, (4) follow-up postmortem if it recurs.
Lee: I'll pin a quick dashboard in Console under Telemetry -> Pipeline Canary.
Priya: note: long-term we should add an attribute budget per span (drop extras beyond N attrs) and implement a shallow sample for high-frequency short sessions.
Noah: logging note: past 2k error lines show "failed export: s3 write slow" intermittently. linking to retention run: https://internal.redwood.tech/infra/retention/jobs/4223
Ashley: thanks. set a 2hr incident watch. if canary keeps improving, rollback routing change as a safety until we have attribute budget change.
Noah: will open a short issue with traces/examples and raw spans attached. filing: ENG-PLAT-5678
Sam: :thumbsup: keep us posted.
Lee: i'll add a small alert on exporter.queue.max_seen > 10k.
Noah: last check (now): exporter.queue.size=2700, process.p99=298ms, cpu host 68%. setting last_message here, follow-ups in ENG-PLAT-5678.
